2.  Learning rate in SGD modulates the speed of learning from mistakes to approach the
   goal of learning. Stiffness in spring determines how fast a spring returns to its equilibrium
    status. When learning rate is high, learning in SGD is fast but may be inaccurate; low,
    learning is slow but accurate. High/low stiffness leads to faster/slower return of spring to
    equilibrium. (Not necessary but acceptable: when the learning rate is high, we may
   observe oscillations in SGD learning process)

3.  Perturbation theory (mass ⬆️frequency ⬇️; stiffness ⬆️frequency ⬆️) The two sides of
    the the basilar membrane are different in mass and stiffness. The longer side is light and
    floppy (low mass and high stiffness) such that it captures high frequency sounds; the
    short side is heavy and dull (high mass and low stiffness) such that it captures low
   frequency sounds. Both sides are connected to the brain by neurons, which is how the
    brain receives such signals of whether we heard a low f or high f sound.

    of the previous neuron and the weight, and then add the inner products up for all the

    to layer, and in the end the output is a probability distribution of all possible outcomes
